chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from his father, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

If a salat (prayer) has been missed by you and you remember it during the time of another, then if you know that when you perform the one that you missed, you will still be within the time of the other, then begin with the one you missed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
"And establish the salat (prayer) for My remembrance."
And if you know that when you perform the one you missed, the one after it will also pass you by, then begin with the one whose time you are in, and perform the other afterward.

key_terms.الَّتِي أَنْتَ فِي وَقْتِهَا: the one whose time you are in; the currently due prayer
key_terms.فَابْدَأْ: then begin; an instruction regarding which prayer to start with
key_terms.فَاتَتْكَ: was missed by you; refers to a prayer whose appointed time passed
key_terms.لِذِكْرِي: for My remembrance; indicating prayer upon remembrance
key_terms.وَقْتِ: time; the legally designated time window for a prayer

ai.seo_question: If I remember a missed prayer during the time of another prayer, which one should I perform first?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the order of performing a missed salat (prayer) when it is remembered during the time of another prayer. If there is enough time, the missed prayer is performed first; if not, the current prayer is performed first, then the missed one. It cites the Qur'anic command to establish prayer upon remembrance as proof for prioritizing the missed prayer when possible.
